name: 16b interpolation versus ntk scaling
title: Position interpolation and NTK-aware scaling on three RoPE pairs
subtitle: Head width 128, base 10,000, trained at 4,096 tokens, served at 131,072 (s = 32)

steps.caption: Pairs 0, 32 and 63 turn by 1, 0.01 and 0.000115 radians per position. Training at 4,096 tokens shows them angles up to 4,095, 41 and 0.47 radians. Pairs 0 and 32 wrap many times, while pair 63 never finishes a turn.

Serving 131,072 tokens with no change pushes pair 63 to 15.1 radians, 32 times the largest angle it saw in training. Pairs 0 and 32 only wrap more often, so every angle they produce is still familiar.
Position interpolation divides every position by 32. Pair 63 tops out at 0.47 radians again, but neighbouring tokens on pair 0 now differ by 1.8 degrees instead of 57.3.
NTK-aware scaling raises the base from 10,000 to 338,097. Pair 0 keeps its rate, pair 32 slows 5.8 times, and pair 63 slows 32 times, so it again tops out at 0.47 radians.

Side by side, interpolation slows the three pairs 32, 32 and 32 times, while NTK-aware scaling slows them 1, 5.8 and 32 times. Both fix the slow pair, and only NTK-aware scaling keeps the fast pair sharp.
